title: Reconcile late-ingest & rate-limit attribution for per-model usage charts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Per-model usage dashboards sporadically show negative dips, duplicate spikes, and mismatched totals after rate-limit events and backfilled/delayed ingestion. Root causes appear to be: (1) the realtime ingestion path attributes token counts to the fallback model when rate-limited, while backfill repairs attribute to the original requested model; (2) late events are rolled into older time buckets without compensating debits for prior overcounts; (3) deduplication between realtime and backfill pipelines is non-deterministic for schema-v1 events. Impact: inaccurate per-model breakdowns in Console, customers seeing billing mismatches and poor trust in model-level unit economics. Goal: produce a deterministic, auditable reconciliation so Console per-model charts and exports match billing and billing-alerting for both realtime and backfilled events.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical per-token attribution chosen and documented; all dashboards use this canonical attribution
Late/backfilled events are applied with idempotent debit/credit semantics so historical time buckets never show negative totals
Realtime vs backfill dedupe implemented using event-hash + ingestion-watermark; test harness added with synthetic delayed events
Dashboard unit tests and integration tests validate reconciliation across scenarios: rate-limit fallback, retry storms, multi-model fanout requests
A runbook describing how to reprocess specific customer ranges is in Confluence and verified by SRE
New metrics emitted: backfill-lag, attributed-discrepancy-count, dedupe-failure-rate
implementation_steps: Define canonical attribution: attribute tokens to original request.model_id (not to fallback) together with an attribute 'served_model' that stores final model that served response
Bump ingestion schema to v2 to include 'origin_request_id' and 'event_fingerprint' for deterministic dedupe
Add watermark-based backfill window policy: events with event_ts < now() - 14d are routed to historical-reprocess topic and processed with debit/credit semantics
Implement idempotent ledger entries in billing-events-v2: each event has (event_fingerprint, amount, credit/debit flag) and reconciliation job applies idempotent operations
Update Console charting pipeline to consume canonicalized per-model aggregates from reconciliation job instead of raw realtime topic
Add unit/integration tests with scenarios: rate-limit triggered with fallback, delayed duplicate arrival, partial-day reprocess, burst retries
Create migration job to re-run last 30 days using new ledger semantics for affected customers; schedule in off-peak with throttling
Instrument dashboards and add alerts for discrepancy > 0.5% between console-aggregates and billing-exports
progress_updates: 2026-02-18: Spike completed to compare attribution between realtime and backfill for a sample tenant. Found 23% of mismatches were due to 'served_model' attribution during 429-handling. (Aisha)
2026-02-22: Design review with PM and Data Eng: agreed on canonical attribution to 'requested_model' and separate 'served_model' field. Decided to prefer ledger approach for idempotency. (Jun)

2026-02-28: Schema v2 PR opened: add origin_request_id + event_fingerprint + credit_flag. PR: github.com/redwood/ingest/pull/4823 (link in related_links). Blocker: Kinesis producer lib needs patch for schema negotiation. (Jun)
2026-03-04: Implemented deterministic dedupe using event_fingerprint; local integration tests show dedupe-failure-rate falling from 4.2% to 0.03% on synthetic data. (Jun)

2026-03-08: Reconciliation job prototype running in staging producing canonical per-model aggregates. Small discrepancy persists for multi-model fanout requests where request-level attribution is ambiguous; working with product to define expected business logic. (Aisha)
2026-03-10: Began scheduling migration job for last 30 days in a gated rollout; SRE requested a soft quota cap during reprocess window to avoid impacting live Dedicated workloads. (Jun)
2026-03-10: Added dashboard metric 'attributed-discrepancy-count' and initial alert on staging (threshold 100 events/day).
decisions: Canonical attribution: attribute billing tokens to the 'requested_model_id' at request creation time. Any fallback/served model is stored as metadata for debugging but not for billing totals.
Use ledger (credit/debit) semantics for applying late events to avoid negative buckets and ensure idempotency across replays.
Schema v2 required: include origin_request_id + event_fingerprint to support deterministic dedupe; older schema events will be reprocessed via migration job.
Backfill window chosen: 14 days for automatic watermark handling; longer ranges will go through controlled reprocess job with SRE coordination.
Console charts will switch to reconciled_aggregates topic as source of truth once reconciliation job has 99.9% coverage and discrepancy alerting is green for 48 hours.
Minor customer-facing discrepancies (<=0.5%) will be noted in a public FAQ while we run migration; major discrepancies will trigger customer outreach via CSMs.
blockers: Kinesis schema negotiation bug in producer library blocks schema-v2 rollout (tracked internally)
Need signoff from Finance on canonical attribution decision before billing exports are updated
Reprocessing job resource limits: require temporary Dedicated capacity quota increases during migration window (coordination with capacity team)
